positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description:
Builds single page web apps for scientific community portals using React, ES6, Jest, SCSS 
Works directly with portal customers to understand their needs and fulfill user requirements
Creates and manages npm library with core components of web portals
Architects templated portal deployment system to streamline development
Integrates npm library with legacy client by bundling library as UMD build using Rollup
Prioritizes emerging best practices (migrating Javascript to Typescript, integrating React hooks)
Contributes to RESTful Java spring backend

positions.title: Software Engineer Intern
positions.description:
Built single page web app for Parkinson's research study consent flow using Vue.js and Bootstrap
Partnered with Design team lead to conduct user interviews and develop user empathy
Incorporated customer feedback to create new iterations of web app in agile environment

positions.title: Undergraduate Intern
positions.description:
Extended Python ML software tool for increased data volume and throughput using AWS
Created software pipeline using S3, EC2, and CloudFormation
Balanced budget constraints of allotted AWS resources

positions.title: Tutor
positions.description:
•	Teaching advanced computer science topics and calculus
•	Mentor incoming freshmen
•	Organizing teaching plans for individuals

positions.title: Undergraduate Researcher
positions.description:
-Conducted a research project studying the occurrence of zinc finger proteins under the guidance of Anton Persikov (PhD) and Mona Singh (PhD)
-Analyzed large data files of zinc finger proteins using Python
-Presented a poster of research findings to fellow colleagues and professors
-Collaborated in open office environment with other graduate students

positions.title: Undergraduate Researcher
positions.description:
•Conducted undergraduate research project studying Prochlorococcus
•Utilized Python scripts to process meta genomic data files
•Used spectrophotometer to analyze stock cultures
•Presented a poster of research findings at Mary Gates Undergraduate Research Symposium
